teams.product_capability: A production-ready OpenCaseLaw retrieval/cache adapter that turns a Swiss legal question into a normalized, provenance-preserving query_result_bundle candidate set for downstream answer generation and mapping.
teams.question: Can OpenCaseLaw's public REST/CLI surface, combined with existing LexMachina caching/search utilities, produce a deterministic high-recall 100–300-decision candidate bundle with multilingual expansion, deduplication, lazy full-text/structure retrieval, and citation-neighborhood expansion without rebuilding a national corpus?
teams.hypothesis: Yes. OpenCaseLaw already exposes relevance-ranked /api/decisions search, full decisions, structured reasoning, citations, leading cases and canonical URLs. A thin adapter plus query expansion, pagination, caching and normalization should replace the old 174k ingestion path for the MVP.
teams.why_now: Human pivot v43 makes owner attention the scarce resource and OpenCaseLaw the canonical source. Public documentation verified 2026-10-11 exposes free/no-key REST search, decision structure, citation graph and leading-case routes. The current product lane already has server/cache/navigation patterns but no query-specific OpenCaseLaw bundle adapter. This is an independent implementation bottleneck that can be built in parallel.
teams.non_duplication: Core product owns end-to-end integration/UI and will consume accepted artifacts; evaluation owns benchmarks. This team owns ONLY the reusable retrieval adapter, fixtures and normalized bundle contract in its Frontier namespace. It must reuse accepted product cache/search patterns rather than build another app shell.
dependencies: OpenCaseLaw public REST API: https://mcp.opencaselaw.ch/api/decisions plus decision/structure/citations/leading-cases endpoints; no API key; soft pace <=5 req/s

Accepted lab/product server/cache/navigation patterns on origin branch lab/product (worktree appears at /tmp/lex_accepted/core/product only while the Product core lane status is RUN; otherwise fetch lab/product directly)
Existing LexMachina multilingual/TF-IDF utilities where directly reusable
teams.acceptance_test: (1) Runnable Python adapter/CLI with live and cached modes. (2) A real Swiss-law query can page/merge OpenCaseLaw results into a normalized bundle with decision_id, canonical_url, citation string, language, date/court, title/regeste/snippet and retrieval provenance; configurable target up to at least 100 results without violating documented rate limits. (3) Deduplication is deterministic by decision_id/canonical identity. (4) Lazy full decision/structure fetching works for selected candidates. (5) Citation-neighborhood expansion can add incoming/outgoing/leading-case candidates with provenance and bounded limits. (6) At least FR/DE/IT query variants or language-filtered expansion are supported without fabricating translations. (7) Cached fixtures make tests deterministic/offline. (8) Tests exercise pagination, cache, dedupe, provenance and remote-failure degradation. (9) A short machine-readable integration contract documents how product imports/copies the adapter.
teams.stop_promote_rule: PROMOTE when acceptance (1)-(9) pass and hand artifacts to product/evaluation. Continue only for concrete adapter defects found by integration. TERMINATE if OpenCaseLaw public interfaces cannot supply stable decision IDs/source URLs/full-text/citation expansion required by the bundle; document exact missing capability instead of rebuilding the national corpus.

teams.product_capability: Provider-agnostic sourced legal answer generation plus an independent counter-authority/adversarial pass that can run for development with a free OpenCode CLI or local model and later swap to production inference.
teams.question: Can a query_result_bundle be turned into a genuinely generative, source-grounded legal answer and then independently challenged for contradictory, limiting, distinguishing or exception authorities, with every surfaced citation constrained to retrieved OpenCaseLaw decision IDs and verifiable against sources?
teams.hypothesis: Yes. The LLM need not be custom-trained; a provider abstraction plus source packing, citation-ID constraints, a separate adversarial retrieval/generation pass and post-generation validation should deliver the required behavior. OpenCaseLaw's verification/attestation routes can strengthen source checks.
teams.why_now: The product's remaining differentiation is not generic chat but an answer that exposes what it may have simplified. This capability is logically independent of rendering and can be implemented/tested in parallel. Development must not require the owner to provision paid APIs, while the future production provider remains replaceable.
teams.non_duplication: Core product owns the final answer panel and server integration; frontier-query-retrieval owns data acquisition; evaluation owns comparative benchmarks. This team owns ONLY the generation/provider abstraction, source-packing/citation validation contract, and adversarial second-pass logic/fixtures.
dependencies: Accepted product/server patterns on origin branch lab/product (worktree appears at /tmp/lex_accepted/core/product only while the Product core lane status is RUN; otherwise fetch lab/product directly)
Free OpenCode model available in CI via current model-health, and/or optional local Ollama/OpenAI-compatible backend for developer machines
OpenCaseLaw decision IDs/canonical URLs and public verification endpoints such as /api/attest when useful
frontier-query-retrieval artifacts may be consumed once ACCEPTED, but this charter must also work against a frozen synthetic/cached bundle fixture so it can proceed independently
teams.acceptance_test: (1) Provider interface with at least one real no-owner-cost development path attempted and working in CI or documented local mode (OpenCode CLI and/or local model), plus deterministic fixture/mock for tests. (2) Given a bundle, generate a substantive answer that cites only decision IDs present in the source bundle; hallucinated IDs are programmatically rejected. (3) Run a logically independent adversarial pass whose objective is to find/flag contradictory, limiting, distinguishing, older/minority or exception authorities; it must not simply restate the first answer. (4) Merge adversarial findings into structured statuses supporting/limiting/contrary_or_exception/unclassified with uncertainty and evidence references. (5) Add post-generation citation/source validation, using OpenCaseLaw attestation/claim support where feasible or strict local bundle validation otherwise. (6) Produce at least one end-to-end cached example with answer + adversarial findings. (7) Tests cover invented citation rejection, unsupported-status downgrade, provider failure fallback and deterministic parsing. (8) Publish a narrow integration contract for product.
teams.stop_promote_rule: PROMOTE when (1)-(8) pass. Continue only for concrete integration defects or source-validation failures. TERMINATE the specific provider path if it cannot produce tool-usable output reliably; keep the provider abstraction and try another free/local development provider without escalating to the owner.

teams.product_capability: A query-specific interactive jurisprudence map that consumes query_result_bundle data and reuses the existing LexMachina WebGL/Canvas/navigation shell, with readable clusters, outliers, relations and counter-authority emphasis.
teams.question: Can the existing LexMachina visual stack be adapted behind a query_result_bundle seam so 100–300 retrieved decisions become a useful clickable map without depending on the old universal 174k alignment/global hierarchy?
teams.hypothesis: Yes. Existing WebGL/Canvas, navigation, cluster/decision-detail and LOD code are already far more than the MVP needs. Replacing the global representation loader with a query-bundle adapter plus local TF-IDF/similarity, deterministic clustering and 2D projection should yield a testable interface quickly.
teams.why_now: The visual audit layer is the product hypothesis the owner wants to test. The old UI/server are valuable sunk work, but current assumptions are global-map oriented. An isolated adaptation prototype can advance in parallel with retrieval and generative work, using cached bundles.
teams.non_duplication: Core product remains integrator. This team owns ONLY the visual/query-bundle adaptation prototype and tests inside its Frontier namespace. It must reuse accepted product frontend/rendering/navigation code where possible rather than redesign branding or create a separate polished app.
dependencies: Accepted lab/product frontend/server/navigation/rendering code on origin branch lab/product (worktree appears at /tmp/lex_accepted/core/product only while the Product core lane status is RUN; otherwise fetch lab/product directly)
Existing LexMachina TF-IDF/clustering/UMAP/Leiden utilities where useful
A frozen 100+ decision fixture may be synthesized from historical accepted data or public OpenCaseLaw responses so the team does not wait on frontier-query-retrieval
teams.acceptance_test: (1) Runnable local prototype or component that consumes a query_result_bundle fixture with roughly 100+ decisions. (2) Points clickable to decision detail/source link. (3) Visible clusters with labels/placeholders derived from bundle data, outliers preserved, fit/reset/search controls functional. (4) Counter-authority/limiting status can be highlighted/toggled. (5) Citation/typed relation edges appear on selection rather than as permanent spaghetti. (6) No dependency on global 174k id→cluster alignment or global hierarchy. (7) Reuse of existing LexMachina renderer/navigation is demonstrated or a concrete reason for isolated replacement is documented. (8) Automated browser/data smoke tests or equivalent verify bundle load, click mapping and status filtering. (9) Integration contract tells product exactly which files/components to absorb.
teams.stop_promote_rule: PROMOTE when (1)-(9) pass. Continue only for concrete usability/integration defects. TERMINATE a rendering approach if it obscures clusters or requires global-174k artifacts; switch to a simpler 2D/Canvas path rather than asking the owner for design decisions.

teams.product_capability: A one-command owner test harness that makes the Master Prompt human product gate answerable in a single sitting: a conventional ranked-list baseline rendered from the SAME query_result_bundle as the map, a one-click list<->map switch over the identical loaded query, the four human-gate questions as a short FR/DE card, and a capture that writes the session's structured claim-bearing record to disk.
teams.question: Can the existing query-map slice be paired with a conventional ranked-list baseline over the SAME query_result_bundle, plus a short owner protocol and a session capture, so that a jurist comparing 'answer + ranked list' against 'answer + map' on the same query produces structured, auditable evidence for the four Master Prompt human-gate questions?
teams.hypothesis: Yes. The bundle already carries decision_id, rank, court, language, decision_date, citation, snippet and canonical_url for every retrieved decision, so a conventional ranked list is a pure re-rendering of data the product already has — no new retrieval, model, corpus or paid service is needed. A view-mode switch, a static test card and a capture routine are a few hundred lines and need no owner provisioning, so the decisive human gate becomes answerable the moment the machine gate turns green instead of weeks later.
teams.why_now: Concrete accepted/observed evidence, not a general idea. (a) The Master Prompt's central product question is comparative ('...better than an AI answer plus a conventional ranked list') and its human product gate names four explicitly comparative questions; without a ranked-list baseline the gate can only be answered subjectively ('do you like the map?'), which the Master Prompt forbids as insufficient. (b) product/static/query.html at lab/product HEAD ea161e6 is 186 lines and contains no ranked-list view and no list/map switch — the only list-like elements are #counterList and #clusterList beside a canvas; verified by reading the file. (c) state/product.json human_gate_criteria lists 'one-command local launch' and 'clickable clusters/outliers/source links' but contains nothing that lets the owner see the conventional baseline or record a structured answer, so an owner session today would produce anecdote rather than claim-bearing evidence. (d) The machine gate is one audit-placement repair away from green (factory direction v50), so the owner session is imminent and unattended owner time must be minimised under the OWNER-ATTENTION doctrine. (e) REUSE-FIRST: query_app.py's two-phase /api/query/start + /api/query/enrich API, the Canvas renderer and the bundle contract already exist; nothing is rebuilt.
teams.non_duplication: frontier-query-map-ui (PROMOTED, PAUSE) owns the map rendering adaptation and must not be rerun. Core product owns integration and is explicitly forbidden by factory direction v50 from building the ranked-list baseline or the owner harness. Core evaluation is PAUSE and owns automated benchmarks; this team must not add synthetic benchmark churn. This team owns ONLY the conventional ranked-list baseline component, the view-mode switch, the owner test card and the session capture inside its own Frontier namespace, and touches no product/ or state/product.json file.

teams.acceptance_test: (1) A runnable ranked-list baseline component in frontier/frontier-human-gate-harness/ that renders the conventional view from a query_result_bundle alone — rank, decision_id, court, date, language, citation, snippet and source link, in the bundle's rank order, adding no map or semantic information (no cluster colour, no proximity, no counter grouping), explicitly labelled as the conventional baseline. (2) A list<->map switch that renders BOTH views from the SAME already-loaded bundle and the SAME query, with no re-retrieval and no bundle mutation, so the A/B comparison is literally the same evidence. (3) An owner test card in FR and DE carrying the four Master Prompt human-gate questions in intent, each with a short scale and a free-text field, plus one suggested real Swiss-law question drawn from the frozen reality-check legs. (4) A capture routine writing a machine-readable session record (results/frontier/frontier-human-gate-harness/session_<id>.json) containing bundle/query hash, view mode per action, decisions opened, counter-authorities opened, timestamped answers to the four questions and wall-clock latency — no personal data, no fabricated entries, no silent defaults for missing answers. (5) A one-command offline path, smoke-tested: python -m frontier_human_gate_harness.cli --fixture <bundle> --out <dir> produces the baseline view, the card and an empty capture with no network access. (6) Deterministic offline tests, at least 8: same fixture -> byte-identical baseline render and capture schema; rendered order equals bundle rank; the switch does not mutate the bundle; the capture rejects a missing answer instead of inventing one. (7) A short integration contract naming the exact files/hooks product must copy to enable the switch in product/static/query.html, stating that product owns final integration and this team owns no product file. (8) Zero writes outside frontier/frontier-human-gate-harness/, tests/frontier/frontier-human-gate...
teams.stop_promote_rule: PROMOTE when (1)-(8) pass and artifacts plus the integration contract are handed to product/evaluation. Continue only for concrete integration defects named by Product/Evaluation. TERMINATE and document instead of inventing data if the bundle lacks the fields a conventional ranked list needs (rank, court, date, language, citation, canonical_url) — report the exact missing bundle field as a product contract defect. Do not escalate design, copy or UX choices to the owner, and do not extend scope into retrieval, generation or benchmark work.
